$comment: Canonical registry of coverage areas for macstack.json (field context.plugins.*[].covers). Answers 'which plugin do I open for this task?' — one shared vocabulary for all projects, checked by the macstack-dev linter. Two kinds: 'section' areas map 1:1 onto sections of the stack file (the plugin teaches you how to build that part of the stack); 'cross-cutting' areas are not tied to a single section. Extension: a new area = a kebab-case slug + a PR to this file (origin: extension).

areas.name: Results
areas.description: How to formulate a result in money and metrics for this stack

areas.name: Processes
areas.description: Business processes, their steps and HITL points

areas.name: Triggers
areas.description: What starts the work: schedule, webhook, db_event, form, queue

areas.name: Workflows
areas.description: Automation bodies — how a process is actually executed in code or in an engine

areas.name: Software
areas.description: The tool itself: how to install, configure and operate this piece of software in the stack

areas.name: Entities
areas.description: Data model: collections, fields, relations, which store is master

areas.name: Interfaces
areas.description: Everything a human or an external system touches: UI, admin panels, bots, notification channels

areas.name: Connections
areas.description: The stack's sockets: MCP servers, direct APIs, CLI access

areas.name: Agents
areas.description: Stack agents and managed agents: hierarchy, delegation, tools

areas.name: Roles
areas.description: Who sees and can do what — the role model of the stack

areas.name: Resources
areas.description: Registry of env keys, external services and data assets

areas.name: Integrations
areas.description: External client systems the stack talks to

areas.name: Deployment & hosting
areas.description: Build, deploy, domains, certificates, rollback

areas.name: Secrets & environment
areas.description: Where secrets live and how they reach every target without drift

areas.name: SEO & discoverability
areas.description: How public interfaces get found: meta, structured data, sitemaps, Core Web Vitals. Distinct from `interfaces`, which is about building them

areas.name: Testing
areas.description: How this stack is tested and what counts as green

areas.name: Observability
areas.description: Logs, metrics, traces, error monitoring, alerts

areas.name: Data migration
areas.description: Schema migrations, backfills, moving data between stands

areas.name: Security & access
areas.description: Authentication, authorization, network access, hardening, backups

areas.name: Conventions
areas.description: Naming, code style, commit and branch discipline for this stack

areas.name: Documentation
areas.description: How the stack documents itself: CLAUDE.md, docs, specs, reports

areas.name: Cost & billing
areas.description: What the stack costs to run and how it charges its own clients
